item.title: Como renews lighting on Viale Varese, 80-thousand-euro project
item.description: The Municipality of Como officially launched the public lighting renewal project along two sections of Varese Avenue.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Municipality of Como renews the lighting on viale Varese - The project is worth 80mila euro overall - 50mila euro are allocated from cross-border funds - The work is expected to be completed in spring 2027
## Key facts - What → renewal of public lighting - Where → two sections of the central reservation on viale Varese - Amount → 80mila euro - Funding → 50mila euro from cross-border funds and 30mila from surplus - Duration → approximately 195 days
The Municipality of Como officially launched the project to renew public lighting along two sections of viale Varese. The city council, led by Mayor Alessandro Rapinese, approved the guidance document for designing the project, declaring the measure immediately enforceable.
The objective indicated by the source is to overcome the frequent breakdowns and inconveniences that often leave motorists and pedestrians in the dark. The construction work will concern the central reservation, that is, the strip separating the traffic lanes from the parking area.
### The scope of the project
The first section concerned lies between piazza Cacciatori delle Alpi and via Borsieri. The second is located between via benzi and viale Cattaneo. The project is therefore limited to two specific segments of the avenue and does not coincide with the replacement of all the lighting in the area.
The system serving the pedestrian green area adjacent to the historic walls is excluded. According to the source, that space has an independent network and decorative fixtures, separate from the system included in the project.
The existing infrastructure has old buried cables without adequate protection or conduits. This configuration prevents maintenance work from being carried out without breaking up the asphalt. The support poles also show corrosion at the base.
The new project provides for the re-excavation of trenches, the installation of conduits and inspection chambers, the construction of foundation footings, and the installation of new electrical lines. It also includes poles, arms and latest-generation LED light fixtures, described as more efficient and higher-performing. The work will be organized in phases to ensure service continuity and road safety during construction. The cost estimate separates expenditure on the works from the technical and financial items. The total investment amounts to 80mila euro. Of this amount, 60mila euro are allocated directly to the works; this item includes 12mila euro for labor and 1.800 euro for safety costs.
The remaining 20mila euro in the cost estimate are allocated to ancillary items: in addition to VAT at 22%, they include reserves for contingencies and price revisions, technical incentives, and internal insurance coverage. This amount is separate from that for the works and does not correspond to a second construction site.
### Reading the amounts
| Item | Amount | Calculated ratio | |---|---:|---:| | Works | 60mila euro | 75% of the 80mila euro | | Labor | 12mila euro | included in the works | | Safety costs | 1.800 euro | included in the works | | Other items in the cost estimate | 20mila euro | 25% of the 80mila euro | | Cross-border funds | 50mila euro | 62,5% of the funding | | Budget surplus | 30mila euro | 37,5% of the funding |
The percentages in the table are calculations based on the reported values: 60mila divided by 80mila gives 75%, while 20mila divided by 80mila gives 25%. For the funding, 50mila out of 80mila corresponds to 62,5%; the 30mila from the surplus corresponds to 37,5%. The total of the two sources comes to 80mila euro.
The figure most directly connected to the cross-border community is therefore the source of 50mila euro in the funding. The text refers to cross-border funds and a budget surplus; in this description, however, it does not attribute the expenditure to an individual deduction or personal payment. The distinction serves to separate a project-funding item from a payslip item.
The design was carried out in-house by the municipal technical office. For execution, the Municipality will award the works to City green Light through an extension of the «Servizio Luce 4» contract. The source therefore separates the design phase, carried out by the administration, from the subsequent implementation entrusted to the indicated operator. The timeline indicated by the source spans approximately one hundred and ninety-five days in total. The starting point is the initial go-ahead in November 2026. After this step, the preparation and approval of the detailed design are planned, followed by the award to the operator and the opening of the construction site. The stated objective is to complete the project by spring 2027.
### From design to construction
The sequence described sets out four stages: detailed design, approval, award and commencement of the works. No calendar with the individual dates for each step is provided. The available timing information therefore remains the overall duration of approximately 195 days and the seasonal target of spring 2027.
Operationally, too, the source defines the general approach but not the day-by-day details. The work will be divided into phases to maintain continuity of service and road safety; however, no schedules, closures or diversions are reported. The text identifies the sections of the avenue and the excluded green area, but does not describe any other affected sections.
For a cross-border worker, the verifiable connection with work across the border remains limited to the line item for cross-border-worker funds allocated to a project in the Municipality of Como. It does not address withholding tax or double taxation. The works are described as being in the Municipality of Como, not in the Canton of Ticino. For the official framework on tax matters concerning cross-border workers, the separate reference is the [AFC information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf), which adds no data on the Viale Varese project.
This distinction also matters when interpreting the reference to cross-border workers in the title: the documented news concerns municipal funding, not a change to tax, social-security or insurance rules. Based on the description, the project remains a public-lighting intervention on two sections of Viale Varese, with its resources, timing and implementation methods indicated only in general terms.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/como-nuova-luce-sara-su-viale-varese-ok-al-progetto-da-80mila-euro-e-pagano-tanto-i-fondi-dei-frontalieri/)*

item.title: Cross-border workers’ salaries in 2027: 1% nominal increase according to UBS
item.description: In 2027, the wages of cross-border workers in Switzerland are expected to increase by 1% in nominal terms.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Nominal wages 2027: 1%; this year they were at 1,1% - Inflation 2027: 0,8%; real wage increase: 0,2% - Energy, supply and recycling: 1,5% - Hotels and restaurants: 0,6%; summer from May 1, 2027
## Key facts - Source → Ubs - Sample → 400 companies - Nominal estimate 2027 → 1% - Forecast inflation 2027 → 0,8% - Seasonal contracts → 30 April 2027 and 1 May 2027
## 2027 wages: the national estimate
In 2027, the wages of cross-border workers in Switzerland are expected to grow by 1% in nominal terms. This is indicated by Ubs's periodic survey, conducted on a representative sample of 400 companies. For the current year, the reported figure is 1,1%: the comparison therefore shows a reduction of 0,1 percentage points in the expected rate.
### From the nominal percentage to the real percentage
The definition used in the source helps interpret the figure: 1% is a nominal increase, that is, calculated before the impact of depreciation. Ubs forecasts inflation of 0,8% for 2027. Subtracting the two values, real wage growth amounts to 0,2%, as indicated by the same estimate. The result remains below the long-term average and below the estimated purchasing-power gain for the current year, equal to 0,4%.
The inflation estimates have been updated. For this year, inflation is expected to average 0,7%, following an upward revision from 0,6% due to higher oil prices. In 2027, the forecast reaches 0,8%, that is, 0,2 percentage points higher than the September estimate. This helps explain why, in Ubs's projections, nominal growth of 1% corresponds to a more limited real increase.
For those working across the border, the distinction between nominal and real is the central point of the update: the first figure concerns the gross increase in remuneration, while the second reflects the result after forecast inflation. However, this is not the same amount for every payslip. The source provides an average for Swiss companies and, as the sectoral distribution shows, does not assign the same percentage to all activities. A breakdown by sector is therefore necessary to interpret the estimate relating to cross-border workers. ## Sectors and minimum wages in tourism
The national average of 1% is only the general reference. Ubs sees a nominal adjustment of 1% in the majority of productive sectors, but points to deviations in some activities. Comparing the percentages reported by the source makes the distance from the average easier to see.
| Sector indicated by Ubs | 2027 estimate | Difference calculated relative to 1% | |---|---:|---:| | Energy, supply and recycling | 1,5% | +0,5 percentage points | | Watchmaking and jewelry | 0,7% | -0,3 percentage points | | Retail trade | 0,8% | -0,2 percentage points | | Tourism, hotels and restaurants | 0,6% | -0,4 percentage points |
Among the sectors with a specified percentage, the difference between the highest and lowest values is therefore 0,9 percentage points. Energy, supply and recycling exceed the average by 0,5 points; watchmaking and jewelry, and retail trade, remain below the national benchmark. These are arithmetic comparisons between estimates, not amounts automatically applicable to every worker.
### The case of Category II
In the tourism sector, and particularly among hotels and restaurants, the increase expected for next year is limited to 0,6%. The source identifies this sector as the one employing a substantial share of Italian cross-border workers. Here, the increase in minimum wages had already been formalized by the social partners and was calibrated to expected inflation.
The joint note cited by the source had been issued by the employers' associations GastroSuisse, HotellerieSuisse and Swiss Catering Association and by the workers' organizations Hotel & Gastro Union, Syna and Unia. For an employee or cross-border worker holding a federal certificate of practical training or an equivalent qualification (Cat. II), the gross monthly salary will rise from 4.070 to 4.094 francs. The increase is therefore 24 gross francs per month.
The agreement allowed the parties to focus on negotiating the new collective labor agreement. The amount indicated is gross and concerns the category described by the source; it does not automatically correspond to the net amount received by every cross-border worker. ## Seasons, health insurance premiums and limits of the forecast
In the case of seasonal contracts, the updated minimum wages will enter into force with the opening of the summer season. The winter period will end no later than April 30, 2027; the summer period will begin the following day, May 1, 2027. The two dates mark the seasonal transition indicated by the source and accompany the application of minimum increases in the sector.
### Health insurance premiums
Ubs analysts link the limited growth in real wages to consumers' spending capacity and also point to the increase in health insurance premiums.
Ubs analysts explain that modest growth in real wages should support consumers' purchasing power only marginally; meanwhile, the average increase in health insurance premiums, estimated at 5% in 2027, reduces disposable income.
The reference to 5% concerns the expected average increase in premiums in 2027. The source does not provide the individual premium of a worker or a specific item on their payslip. The analysts' assessment therefore remains distinct from the estimate of 1% for salaries and the actual calculation of 0.2%.
### What is not included in the estimate
Ubs's survey is not a simulation of net pay and does not provide a local breakdown of the 400 companies. Nor does it indicate how many companies in the sample are located in Canton Ticino. These elements therefore cannot be used to convert the average salary into an individual's net pay or to attribute a specific result to a single cross-border commuter.
For the tax framework that the source does not develop, the [FTA information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf) is the official reference listed among the verified data; the document remains separate from the wage survey. For a numerical comparison of the gross change in one's own situation, payslip simulator is available.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/tipendi-svizzera-2027-aumenti-frontalieri-ubs/)*

item.title: Cross-border workers: increase in Switzerland, annual decline in Ticino
item.description: In the third quarter, the cross-border commuter statistics highlight a clear contrast between the federal situation and that of Canton Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 414’500 workers with a G permit in the third quarter - In Ticino, 79’400 people, 0,3% fewer than in 2025 - Switzerland grows by 1,8% year-on-year - Services account for 289’300 employees, +2,3%
## Key facts - Period → third quarter - Switzerland → 414’500 workers with a G permit - Ticino → 79’400 people - France → 58% of domiciled cross-border workers - Italy → 22% of domiciled cross-border workers
In the third quarter, cross-border worker statistics highlight a clear contrast between the federal situation and that of the Canton of Ticino. According to data published by the Federal Statistical Office (UST) and reported by Keystone-ATS, at the federal level there were 414’500 workers with the so-called G permit, an increase of 1,8% year on year. South of the Alps, by contrast, there were 79’400, down 0,3% compared with the same period of 2025.
The federal change is positive, while the Ticino change is negative: there is a difference of 2,1 percentage points between the two rates, calculated by comparing 1,8% with the 0,3% decrease. For those following cross-border employment, the comparison makes clear that the Swiss total cannot be used as a snapshot of Canton Ticino alone, just as the figure south of the Alps does not represent the Confederation as a whole.
### Two geographical scales
| Area | Number in the third quarter | Change | |---|---:|---| | Switzerland | 414’500 workers | +1,8% year on year | | Ticino, south of the Alps | 79’400 people | 0,3% less than in the same period of 2025 |
The two rows belong to the same third quarter and use the same category of workers, namely holders of the G permit, but the source does not present the national change as an effect of the Ticino figure. The text offers no cause for the decrease in Ticino or explanation for the simultaneous federal increase. Limiting oneself to the data avoids turning an observed difference into an undocumented causal relationship. For a cross-border worker, the key to interpreting the figures is therefore the scale: the national number is rising, while the Ticino figure indicated by the source is declining by 0,3% in the year-on-year comparison. ## National growth has several components
Looking at the Confederation as a whole, 58% of all cross-border workers were domiciled in France. The share referring to Italy was 22%, while Germany’s reached 16%. The arithmetic sum of the three percentages is 96%; the source does not describe the remainder. The Italian figure is therefore a share referring to Switzerland as a whole and does not automatically coincide with the count of 79’400 people in Ticino. This distinction avoids overlapping the national distribution of places of residence with the figures for the area south of the Alps.
Over a longer period, the text notes that in just five years the number of workers increased by 58’000, rising by 17%. The five-year comparison broadens the perspective relative to the year-on-year change, but does not show how the increases were distributed from one year to the next.
In the third quarter, the Lake Geneva region is identified as one of the areas driving growth: +3,0% to 169’200. The source reports +3,0%, that is, 3% in equivalent form; compared with the federal 1,8%, the change is higher by 1,2 percentage points. This is an arithmetic comparison between rates, not a cause indicated by the source.
The sectoral breakdown adds another difference: services accounted for 289’300 employees, +2,3% in one year; the secondary sector 122’100, +0,6%.
| Area | Number | Change | |---|---:|---:| | Lake Geneva region | 169’200 | +3,0% | | Services | 289’300 employees | +2,3% | | Secondary sector | 122’100 employees | +0,6% |
The difference between +2,3% and +0,6% is 1,7 percentage points. The arithmetic sum of the two sectoral counts is 411’400; the source does not assign the missing 3’100 relative to the federal total to a specific sector. The picture thus shows where growth is more intense, without establishing why. ## The scope of the survey
The informational value of the UST survey depends on its precise scope: it counts workers with the so-called G permit, captures the third quarter and compares both the previous year and a five-year period. These bases are not interchangeable. The 17% does not describe the change in each year: the source provides the overall result for the five-year period, not the intermediate trajectory.
The same limitation applies to sectors and regions. The UST indicates the Lake Geneva region, services and the secondary sector, but does not explicitly link those data to the contraction in Ticino. No cause is indicated for the nationwide 1,8%, nor for the 0,3% decrease south of the Alps. Any interpretation beyond this point would be an undocumented deduction.
### Separating statistics and taxation
The count does not measure withholding tax, the New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement or double taxation. These tax aspects are not examined in the statistical text. For tax matters, the official reference is the [AFC information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf); this reference concerns tax rules, not UST figures on workers with a G permit.
The breakdown by place of residence also remains descriptive: it indicates France, Italy and Germany, but does not associate these shares with the Canton of Ticino alone. For a cross-border commuter, the verifiable relationship therefore remains limited: the statistics show a territorial divergence and a national composition by place of residence and sector, but do not document any further effects on working conditions.
*Source: [tvsvizzera.it](https://www.tvsvizzera.it/tvs/frontalieri%3a-forte-aumento-in-svizzera%2c-calo-annuo-in-ticino/92356558)*

item.title: 13th AVS payment for Italian pensioners starting in December 2026
item.description: A retiree who was a cross-border worker, is enrolled in the Swiss social security system and receives a full AVS pension of 2’520 francs per month
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The 13th AVS payment in Italy will start in December 2026 - 225’316 AVS beneficiaries reside in Italy - The annual flow will exceed 1,7 billion francs - The reform received 58,2% of the votes
## Key facts - Benefit → thirteenth AVS monthly payment - First disbursement → December 2026 - Complete annuity in the example → 2,520 francs per month - AVS beneficiaries in Italy → 225,316 - Additional annual outlay → approximately 132 million francs
## An additional monthly payment also for those living in Italy
A pensioner who has been a cross-border worker, is registered in the Swiss social security system and receives a full AVS pension of 2,520 francs per month, will receive an identical sum as a thirteenth month's salary. The first disbursement is scheduled for December 2026. The case described by the source concerns a complete annuity and quantifies the additional amount linked to that benefit at 2,520 francs.
### The audience of beneficiaries
According to statistical data from the UFAS, 225,316 beneficiaries of an AVS pension currently reside in Italy. The group of former workers domiciled in the Peninsula constitutes the main share of pensioners abroad linked to the Swiss Confederation system and represents a quarter of all AVS pensioners residing outside Swiss borders.
The audience described does not only include Italian citizens. It also includes Swiss citizens who have chosen Italy to spend their retirement and workers of other nationalities who, having completed their activity in Switzerland, have chosen Italy as their permanent place of residence. For the majority component, the path is that of an Italian person who worked across the border, paid Swiss social security contributions and returned home at the end of his career.
### Money and calendar
During 2025, Swiss coffers paid approximately 1.59 billion francs in ordinary AVS pensions to pensioners resident in Italy. With the entry into force of the thirteenth month's salary, the annual flow to Italy will exceed 1.7 billion francs. The additional annual outlay is estimated at approximately 132 million francs and, according to the source, will be allocated entirely to pensioners domiciled in Italy.
UFAS spokesperson Harald Sohns confirmed:
> «Beneficiaries resident in Italy will also receive the new benefit in full».
The reform, approved in the federal vote in March 2024 with 58.2% of the favorable votes of the people and the cantons, therefore brings the new benefit beyond the Swiss borders. The financial data concerns the total annuities transferred to Italy; the example of 2,520 francs concerns a single complete annuity. The first is an aggregate data, the second an individual example: the first disbursement is scheduled for December 2026. ## A full pension and an average pension are not the same figure
The figure of 2’520 francs per month does not correspond to the average pension of beneficiaries residing in Italy. The source uses that amount to illustrate the case of a pensioner with a full pension. For the group as a whole, however, UFAS data show a much lower average: in December 2025, 588 francs per month, equivalent to approximately 630 euros. The comparison therefore requires not conflating an individual example with an aggregate average.
### Comparison of the figures
| Item | Amount | Period or condition | |---|---:|---| | Full pension in the example | 2’520 CHF per month | Pensioner who was formerly a cross-border worker | | Average AVS pension for residents in Italy | 588 CHF per month, approximately 630 euros | December 2025 | | Theoretical minimum pension | 1’260 CHF per month | Complete contribution record of 44 years | | Average AVS pension in the territory of the Confederation | 1’874 CHF per month, approximately 2’015 euros | Monthly average |
The average pension paid in Italy is therefore below the theoretical minimum pension provided for those with a complete contribution record of 44 years. The average figure given for the territory of the Confederation is also higher than the 588 francs recorded in Italy. For the Swiss average, the source gives the monthly amount but does not tie the figure to a date other than the one reported for residents in Italy.
UFAS links the difference to contribution history. Most pensioners residing in Italy have completed only a fraction of their working careers in Switzerland. The amount awarded is therefore determined according to the years for which contributions were paid across the border. For most recipients, the Swiss pension constitutes a supplementary component alongside the benefits accrued in the Italian INPS social security system.
This explanation clarifies why residence in Italy and having previously been a cross-border worker are not, by themselves, enough to identify a full pension. The source documents the relationship between contribution period and amount, but does not provide a breakdown of the 225’316 beneficiaries by years worked in Switzerland.
### What can be quantified about the thirteenth payment
Regarding the new payment, the text gives a precise amount for the full-pension case: 2’520 additional francs. It also confirms that the benefit will be paid in full to beneficiaries residing in Italy as well. However, it does not provide an individual formula for partial pensions or the exact amount of the thirteenth payment corresponding to the average of 588 francs. Therefore, the amount of 2’520 francs cannot be presented as a universal amount for all pensioners residing in Italy. ## The audience does not coincide with a single work history
The 225,316 beneficiaries resident in Italy are not presented by the source as a homogeneous group in terms of citizenship or career. The majority component is made up of Italian citizens who have worked in Switzerland for periods of varying duration, paid Swiss contributions and then returned to their homeland. The source links the allocation to years of contributions, but does not indicate how many years each beneficiary has accumulated.
A second category is made up of Swiss citizens who have chosen Italy for their retirement. For this choice, the text refers to the geographical proximity, the favorable climate and an average lower cost of living compared to the Confederation. The third includes former workers of other nationalities who, once they finished working in Switzerland, permanently established their residence in Italy. The resident data therefore includes multiple profiles and is not presented as a count of former Italian cross-border workers only.
### The reform and the data that aren't there
According to the source, the thirteenth AVS was born from a federal vote in March 2024. The people and the cantons approved it with 58.2% of votes in favour, despite the contrary opinion of the Federal Council and the majority of the Swiss Parliament. The text links the new payment to that decision, but does not report the regulatory text of the reform or describe the financing mechanisms in detail. Instead, it quantifies the additional annual outlay intended for residents in Italy and the overall flow of income, without dividing them by nationality, career or individual amount.
This distinction avoids turning an aggregate estimate into a personal amount. The source documents the first disbursement in December 2026 and the inclusion of beneficiaries resident in Italy; does not provide a table with the amount of the thirteenth for each level of annuity. The connection with INPS is also described as a supplement for most holders, but is not quantified for each individual pensioner.
For the institutional reference on the 2026 AVS framework, the [2026 AVS synoptic table] is available (https://www.ahv-iv.ch/p/2.01.i). These themes cannot be used to calculate the thirteenth or to add effects on the case described, because they are not covered in the text.
To consult the annuity tool, use pension calculator

item.title: Against a VAT increase: a tax that weighs more heavily on those who have less
item.description: The position of the Communist Party does not call into question the payment of the thirteenth pension.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The No side contests the VAT increase - The vote is scheduled for November 29 - The PC indicates an average of 180 francs annually per household - The 13th AVS pension payment will be paid starting in December
## Key facts - Who → PC, VPOD, SISA and young left-wing parties - Where → Bellinzona - When → November 29th - Amount → 180 francs per year per household - AVS profits → over 10 billion in total in 2024 and 2025 - AVS assets → more than 60 billion francs - Effective date → December and subsequent years
### The Bellinzona conference On Monday morning, in Bellinzona, the Communist Party, the VPOD Trade Union, the SISA Trade Union, the Socialist Youth, the Young Greens, the Communist Youth and the Workers' and People's Party presented the reasons for the No to the initiative on the VAT increase intended to finance the thirteenth AVS. The vote is scheduled for November 29th.
The position of the Communist Party does not question the provision of the thirteenth annuity. The party claims that the payment will begin in December and continue in the following years, regardless of the outcome of the VAT vote. The target of the conference is therefore the financing method indicated in the initiative, not the existence of the service.
### The cost indicated for households After the 2024 increase, a new increase in VAT would, according to the PC, lead to an average additional cost of 180 francs per year for each household. This is the average indicated by the party for a household economy; the source does not provide an amount for the individual consumer.
Even keeping the reduced rate unchanged, the party adds, the increase would continue to affect various daily expenses. Those mentioned include clothing, fuel and various services. However, the source does not indicate the share attributable to each item.
The annual number allows only an arithmetic calculation: 180 francs divided by twelve months is equivalent to 15 francs per month. It is not a new estimate of the PC, nor an individual forecast, but the conversion of the average value reported in the news.
The conference therefore defined the topic in terms of average costs for households, not an equal amount for each person. The text does not contain the composition of the average, the reference incomes and a separate calculation for clothing, fuel or services. The value remains the one indicated by the PC as an annual average, without a table of individual cases. ## A comparison: consumption and wages The most concrete comparison offered by the source concerns the basis of the funding. In the arguments put forward by the Giovani Verdi, the VAT increase is described as a regressive tax that weighs proportionally more heavily on low incomes. The alternative indicated by the PC instead relies on payroll contributions. The difference is therefore between two explicitly named bases: consumption on the one hand, salary on the other.
### The two approaches | Element | VAT increase | Payroll contributions | |---|---|---| | Indicated basis | Daily expenses, including clothing, fuel and various services | Salary | | Criterion described | Expenses affected by the increase even with the reduced rate unchanged | Contributions proportional to salary | | Allocation | The source does not indicate an allocation among parties | Half financed by employers | | Relationship to the pension | Financing of the 13th AVS pension payment through the initiative | According to the PC, without burdening the pensions of those who have already paid contributions |
The source specifies that the proposal for payroll contributions takes up the approach initially supported by the promoters of the 13th AVS pension payment. The PC presents it as a way to distribute any additional funding needs in proportion to salary, with half of the contributions borne by employers. The source does not, however, quantify the contribution required or show how the levy would change for individual salary brackets.
The second comparison concerns progressivity. The Giovani Verdi argue that people with a low income spend almost all of their earnings on daily consumption and, consequently, pay tax on a substantial share of their income. People with high incomes, by contrast, can save a larger share and, proportionally, contribute less. They add that even reduced rates for some essential goods would not eliminate the greater tax burden for those with less.
> «It is not a no to the 13th pension payment, but a no to those who want to make those who have less pay for it».
The SISA statement sums up the political line set out at the conference. It does not argue that the 13th pension payment should be scrapped: it objects to the financing having to come through VAT. No individual simulation can be derived from the text, nor can a comparison be made between the cost for a specific household and the alternative payroll contribution. The verifiable fact is the different basis indicated by the two options. ## The other issues raised by the Communist Party
### Profits, assets and urgency To argue that there is no financial urgency, the PC cites two figures relating to the AVS: more than 10 billion francs in total profits recorded in 2024 and 2025, and assets exceeding 60 billion. These figures are presented by the party in support of its position; the source contains neither a separate verification nor an annual breakdown of the profits. The text therefore allows the total for the two years and the asset threshold to be reported, but not to assign them a breakdown by individual year.
The same argument distinguishes financing the thirteenth payment from the discussion of the retirement age. The PC rejects the idea that accepting the VAT increase could prevent a future increase in the retirement age. According to the party, this will remain a demand of right-wing forces regardless of the outcome on November 29. The political conclusion expressed is that any increase in the retirement age should be opposed regardless of the outcome of the vote.
This passage is an assessment by the Communist Party, not an announcement of a decision already taken. The source indicates neither a concrete proposal on the retirement age nor a timetable for discussing it. The documented fact is the connection that the PC rejects: for the party, voting on VAT would not settle the question of the retirement age.
### The scope for cross-border workers The text concerns the vote on VAT and the thirteenth AVS payment in Ticino political coverage. Consequently, the source does not provide an individual amount for a cross-border worker or a specific effect on these matters. The only explicit focus remains the AVS and the way in which the No camp proposes to finance its thirteenth payment.
Among the separate official references for the general framework of pension provision is the [2026 AVS overview table](https://www.ahv-iv.ch/p/2.01.i); this news item, however, does not use that table to add figures or rules to the debate. To learn more about pensions without confusing the vote on VAT with other matters, consult pension calculator.

item.title: Final approval for the construction of the tram-train
item.description: The Federal Court rejects the appeal of three private individuals.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Court dismisses the appeal of three private individuals. - The case concerns the priority stage of the Tram-train. - The first walls were laid in Manno on 29 October. - The Dt speaks of an important step forward.
## Key facts - → Appeal decision rejected by the Federal Court - Applicants → three private individuals - Object of the priority → stage of the Lugano Tram-Train Network - Suspensive effect → application not accepted in June - Preliminary work → ceremony and first walls in Manno on 29 October
The Federal Court rejected the only appeal filed against the realization of the priority stage of the Lugano Train Network. The confirmation, the news reports, came from the Department of the Territory, which attributes to the ruling the final approval of the implementation of the project.
### The sequence of the procedure
On May 11, three private individuals had submitted the censure to the High Court. The censorship also included the request to refer the proceedings to the Federal Administrative Court for further investigation of the appellants' properties. However, the text specifies that the main infrastructure works planned had not been contested.
The distinction is decisive to read the outcome without enlarging the content of the appeal. The judicial initiative concerned the applicants' properties and the requested referral to the Taf; it is not described as an opposition to the main infrastructure works of the priority stage. The data therefore delimits the perimeter of the pronunciation reported by the Department of the territory.
A previous step had concerned the suspensive effect. In June, the Federal Court had not granted the application, thus allowing the preliminary work to proceed. The official start was marked in Manno on 29 October, with a ceremony and the laying of the first walls.
The chronology distinguishes two moments: on the one hand, the preliminary progress already allowed after the decision on the suspension, on the other hand, the rejection of the only appeal, which has now arrived. For the Dt, the result is "an important step forward" in the process of a priority and crucial work for Ticino. According to the same source, the project will halve travel times and alleviate mobility difficulties in Lugano, throughout the Malcantone and in the lower Vedeggio Valley. The news finally links the work to an important funding from the Confederation, without indicating the amount. The most precise way to assess the scope of the judgment is to compare the procedural sequence with that of the works. The first part of the appeal of 11 May and passes from the application for suspensive effect not granted in June. The second coincides with the official start of the preliminaries, marked in Manno on 29 October by a ceremony during which the first walls were laid. The judgment now reported by the Department of the Territory intervenes on this path after the preliminary phase had already been able to proceed.
### Two floors not to be confused
| Step | What the source reports | |---|---| | Appeal | Only appeal of three individuals to the priority stage | | Question | Referral of the deeds to the Taf for further information on the properties | | Suspensive | Not accepted in June by the Tf | | Construction site | Preliminary work started with the first walls in Manno on 29 October |
This reading highlights a concrete comparison: the appeal and the suspension belong to the judicial level, while the laying of the first walls belongs to the operational level. The source does not present them as the same act. The current rejection concerns the appeal; the preliminary initiation had previously been possible precisely because the request for suspension had not been accepted.
The object of the dispute must also be kept distinct from the work as a whole. The three individuals requested new insights into their properties and the referral of the deeds to the Federal Administrative Court. However, the news specifies that the main infrastructure works planned had not been contested. In the facts reported, therefore, the procedure is not described as a challenge to the entire infrastructural content of the priority stage.
For mobility, the source offers a precise indicator but not a complete measurement: it indicates travel times halved as an effect of the project. It does not provide an initial duration and a final duration in minutes, nor does it quantify individual users or savings. The reference area includes the city of Lugano, the Malcantone in its entirety and the lower Vedeggio Valley. As for a border worker who moves to work in the Canton of Ticino, the documented interest remains linked to these areas and the mobility objective indicated by the Dt, not to an individual benefit already measured at the source. The verdict and the funding should be read with the same caution. The news says that the project benefits from significant funding from the Confederation, but does not provide the amount, allocation, disbursement date or overall cost. These details are separate from a judicial authorization: the rejection of the appeal makes the approval described by Dt final, but does not add figures to the funding.
The halving of travel times is also presented as an effect of the project, not as an already available measurement. The text does not indicate a date of entry into service, a current duration to compare with the future one, frequencies, stops, fares or a completion date for the work. This article therefore cannot provide an individual calculation of the time saved, nor a complete operating schedule.
### The scope of the news
For the cross-border commuter, the documented link therefore remains that of mobility in the Canton of Ticino, with reference to the city of Lugano, the whole of Malcantone and the lower Vedeggio Valley. The source does not extend the ruling to employment or cross-border taxation issues. Refunds, withholding tax, Brogeda, INPS, New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement or double taxation are not addressed.
This limitation prevents attributing effects on those issues to the rejection of the appeal. The verifiable result remains more limited: an appeal by three private individuals was rejected, preliminary works had already begun in Manno on October 29 last year, the Department of Territory refers to final clearance and indicates halved travel times as the objective of the project. The rest would require further information beyond the source.
For further information on the specific issue of public transport connections in Ticino: Ticino public transport

item.description: The interview focuses on financing the 13th pension payment through two elements that the source presents together: the solution identified
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Baume-Schneider considers the solution balanced - The funding concerns the AVS thirteenth pension payment - The increase in VAT is 0,4 percentage points - If the no vote prevailed, the first pillar would enter a deficit spiral
## Key facts - Protagonist → Elisabeth Baume-Schneider - Subject → financing of the 13th pension payment - Instrument → VAT increase - Amount → 0,4 percentage points - Assessment → balanced, fair and consistent - Indicated scenario → deficit spiral of the first pillar
The interview focuses on financing the 13th pension payment through two elements that the source presents together: the solution identified and the scenario associated with a possible no vote. Elisabeth Baume-Schneider considers the solution balanced and describes the effort required by the VAT increase as fair and consistent. Her assessment does not replace the figure: the indicated increase is 0,4 percentage points.
The figure should be understood for what it is. It expresses a change in percentage points, not a franc amount for a single family. The text contains no calculation base, application period or income simulation; therefore, the verifiable comparison remains between the numerical measure and the assessment of its moderation for households with low incomes. The text does not turn the increase into a spending forecast: it records the measure and reports the political assessment of it.
### The political issue
The source then presents a specific condition: if the no vote prevailed, the first pillar would, according to Baume-Schneider, enter a deficit spiral. This is a consequence stated in the interview, not a quantified result in the text. The reference to the AVS and its Fund defines the scope of the news. For a cross-border reader in the Canton of Ticino, the reference here is therefore the AVS: the source does not indicate individual amounts, effects on the payslip or changes to other pension arrangements. ## The comparison enabled by the data
The strongest relationship is not between two rates, because the source provides only one: the increase in VAT of 0,4 percentage points. The possible comparison is between that value and the characterization given to households with low incomes. Baume-Schneider describes the increase as, all things considered, moderate for that group; the sentence defines the group under consideration and does not warrant automatically extending the same assessment to every household.
### Measure, judgment and scenario
The words used in the interview also serve different functions. Balanced describes the overall solution for financing the thirteenth pension payment. Correct and coherent describes the effort required by the increase in VAT. Moderate, by contrast, concerns its assessment from the perspective of households with low incomes. They are three judgments about the same arrangement, not three separate amounts. Separating them avoids turning a political assessment into an individual calculation.
A second comparison concerns the AVS Fund and the first pillar. The former is the destination to which, in the wording reported, the franc is directed; the latter is the area that, in the event of a no vote, Baume-Schneider sees entering a deficit spiral. The source therefore links the destination of the resource to the condition of the first pillar, but does not provide a figure to measure that relationship.
The condition remains hypothetical: the text says what would happen if the no vote passed, without indicating an outcome that has already occurred, a duration for the spiral, or an amount for the deficit. This is the limitation of the comparison and also its most precise data point: the source sets out a choice, a measure and a warning, not a historical series. ## The documented perimeter
The title of the source presents every franc allocated to the Avs Fund as an unparalleled solidarity contribution. The sentence does not indicate an additional amount, an individual fee or a calculation formula. Expresses the opinion with which the payment into the Avs Fund is presented; the quantitative data reported in the interview instead remains the VAT increase of 0.4 percentage points.
### What the source does not quantify
An application date, a vote result, a more detailed description of the solution and an estimate in francs of the effect on low-income households are missing. There is also a lack of elements to translate the judgment on the thirteenth month into an amount referring to a single recipient. For this reason, the formula on the deficit spiral must be attributed to the Baume-Schneider declaration and not transformed into an autonomous numerical forecast.
For the cross-border worker from the Canton of Ticino, the news therefore allows us to isolate only the reference to the AVS. It does not document changes for the G permit, LPP, KVG, refunds, withholding tax, the New Cross-Border Agreement or double taxation. These topics cannot be used to derive an effect from the interview on the individual's paycheck, commute or social security position.
For an institutional reference on social security, the [AVS synoptic table 2026] is available (https://www.ahv-iv.ch/p/2.01.i). To delve deeper into the topic of income, AVS/LPP and pension.

item.title: Living in Magreglio and working in Ticino as a border worker
item.description: Analysis and practical information for those who choose to reside in Magreglio, in the province of Como, and work as a border worker in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Residence in Magreglio, in the province of Como according to ISTAT codes - Work activity in Ticino according to the official UST nomenclature - Tax management according to the New Frontier Workers Agreement L. 83/2023 - Specific rules for withholding tax, AHV/AVS and personal income tax (IRPEF) allowance
## Key facts - Italian location: Magreglio, CO province - Work destination: Ticino - Regulatory reference: Law 83 of 13/6/2023 - Agreement entry into force: January 1, 2024 - IRPEF allowance for new cross-border workers: 10,000 euros
Choosing to reside in an Italian municipality like Magreglio, located in the province of Como, and then commuting daily to work in Swiss territory, specifically in Canton Ticino, requires a careful analysis of the logistical, administrative and fiscal factors that regulate the lives of commuting workers. From a territorial perspective, Magreglio represents a characteristic geographical location of the Lombardy pre-Alpine belt, whose travel towards the Swiss border requires navigating road sections and border crossings well known to commuters. For those undertaking this working path, understanding the current regulatory framework is essential to navigate between both Italian and Swiss tax obligations. The provisions introduced by the recent regulatory framework redefine the taxation and social security management methods for those who regularly cross the border. The Swiss Federal Tax Administration FTA and competent bodies define the deductions applied directly at source on dependent employment income earned in Switzerland. For a worker who maintains their official residence in Magreglio and performs their duties in Ticino, daily commuting involves evaluating travel times and available road connections. The analysis of the departure territory and the destination territory allows for better planning of travel, taking into account the specificities of the road links connecting the province of Como with the Swiss customs offices. ### Regulatory and territorial aspects of commuting between Magreglio and Ticino When considering moving to or residing in Magreglio with an annexed job in Ticino, it is necessary to examine precisely the distinction between the regulations applicable to cross-border workers. The classification of workers is based on rigorous criteria established by bilateral agreements and ratification laws, including Law 83 of June 13, 2023, which transposed the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement signed on December 23, 2020, and entered into force on July 17, 2023, with application from January 1, 2024. This regulatory framework distinguishes so-called new cross-border workers from old cross-border workers, regulated by Article 9 of the same agreement. Workers who reside in municipalities located within the established boundaries and who return daily to their homes in Italy are subject to differentiated tax regimes. For new cross-border workers, Switzerland applies a withholding tax of up to 80%, while Italy proceeds to tax the same income by eliminating double taxation through the tax credit mechanism included in the CE section of the 730 tax model. For old cross-border workers, on the other hand, taxation remains limited exclusively to Switzerland according to the parameters defined by the Agreement and transitional provisions. The Convention against Double Taxation, signed on March 9, 1976, constitutes a further reference pillar for the regulation of fiscal relations between Italy and Switzerland, always bearing in mind that the Swiss Confederation is not part of the European Union or the European Economic Area. ## The Swiss social security and contributions context The exercise of an employed activity in the Canton of Ticino entails mandatory registration in the social security and social security systems of the Helvetic Confederation. For the worker residing in Magreglio and employed across the border, the pay slip reflects a series of mandatory contribution deductions established by federal legislation and administered by the competent bodies. These include contributions for Old Age and AVS Survivors Insurance, AI Disability Insurance and IPG Loss of Earnings Allowances, which provide a share to be paid by the employee of 5.3%. To these deductions are added the contributions for AD and AC unemployment insurance set at 1.1% up to the maximum income limit set at 148,200 Swiss francs, as well as the LAINF accident insurance, whose occlusion rate generally varies between 0.7% and 1.5%. A further relevant social security element is the LPP professional pension, whose contributions vary between 7% and 18% based on the age groups starting from the age of twenty-five. The management of these social security institutions requires the utmost attention from the worker, who must coordinate his Swiss contribution position with the social security and tax obligations in force in Italy. The determination of the taxes due in Italian territory takes into account the exemptions provided for by the legislation, such as the IRPEF exemption set at 10,000 euros for new cross-border commuters. As regards health care and medical coverage, cross-border workers working in Ticino can exercise the right of option for KVG health insurance, choosing between the Swiss and Italian systems according to the provisions in force. The deductibles for adults under the KVG regime usually vary between 300 and 2500 Swiss francs. To learn more about economic planning and estimating your net salary in relation to these deductions, you can consult the tax calculator available online. ## Analysis of the labor market and flows of cross-border workers between Italy and Switzerland The phenomenon of cross-border workers between Italy and the Canton of Ticino represents a structural and economically significant component of the regional and cross-border job market. According to statistical data released by the Statistics Office of the Canton of Ticino USTAT, in the first quarter of 2026 there were approximately 79,000 cross-border workers active in Ticino, specifically 78,561 units, highlighting a slight decline compared to previous periods but still remaining at a percentage equal to approximately 32% of the total employed in the Canton of Ticino. This significant presence of manpower from Italian border provinces, including the province of Como where Magreglio is located, has a profound impact on daily mobility, local services and the management of road flows towards the main transit crossings such as Brogeda and Gaggiolo. The administrative collaboration between the Italian and Swiss authorities makes use of official institutions and bodies such as the Federal Tax Administration AFC, the Ministry of Economy and Finance MEF, INPS and the Revenue Agency, which supervise the correct application of tax rules and the transfer of financial resources deriving from tax refunds to border municipalities. For those who live in Magreglio and evaluate professional opportunities in Ticino, the in-depth knowledge of the statistical data and employment dynamics published by bodies such as the Federal Statistics Office BFS and the Secretariat of State for the Economy SECO offers a stable and verifiable information framework. To find your way around the various employment opportunities and better understand the dynamics of the cross-border job market, it is useful to consult the job offers available via the page dedicated to job offers.

item.title: SMILE: sustainable mobility between Varese, Como and Ticino
item.description: On November 10, 2026, Chiasso will be the venue for SMILE’s public presentation.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - SMILE connects Varese, Como and Canton Ticino - Focus on home-work and home-school - Conference in Chiasso on 10 November 2026 - Six meetings between late November and early December
## Key facts - Project → SMILE, light cross-border mobility - Area → provinces of Varese and Como, Canton of Ticino - Leader → Province of Varese and Canton of Ticino - Event → Chiasso, 10 November 2026 - Participation → free with online registration
### The project and its area On November 10, 2026, Chiasso will be the public presentation point of SMILE. The conference will illustrate the official path of the cross-border initiative, the first cognitive results and the territorial analyzes already conducted. The day will also serve to encourage direct dialogue with stakeholders in the border area.
The program includes territorial analysis reports, strategic objectives and operational macro-lines that will guide the common strategy and the first pilot actions. The event is therefore presented as the first public passage of a project intended to involve local bodies, institutions and realities.
SMILE aims to promote more sustainable, accessible and widely integrated mobility in the area between the provinces of Varese and Como and the Canton of Ticino. The initiative focuses on daily mobility, with particular attention to home-work and home-school travel.
At the basis of the project is the need to resolve the historical difficulties of cross-border mobility. The territory is affected every day by an impressive flow of traffic, generated not only by work and study, but also by tourism and leisure. According to the project description, this flow contributes significantly to the constant congestion of the main road axes between Italy and the Swiss Confederation.
The two lead bodies are the Province of Varese and the Canton of Ticino. The direct partnership includes the Regional Transport Commission of Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio, indicated by the acronym CRTM, as well as the Municipality of Como and the Province of Como. Furthermore, the project receives operational support from numerous associated municipalities and local authorities.
The approach is divided between supply and demand for mobility. On the one hand, routes, spaces and services for bicycles, walking and integration between public transport and cycle mobility are planned. On the other hand, the aim is to stimulate citizens' knowledge, sensitivity and propensity towards sustainable, interconnected and virtuous methods.
Finally, the project includes a cross-border action plan for the development of light mobility. Planning will start from the analysis of the state of the art, demand volumes and emerging trends. This phase will be accompanied by pilot actions on infrastructures, spaces, cycling services and information, training and awareness initiatives aimed at workers, students, residents and visitors to the area. ## From shared vision to action on the ground
### Supply, demand and planning SMILE connects three distinct levels: how people travel, what the area offers and the process by which priorities will be defined. The source therefore describes not only the construction or modernization of routes. Alongside infrastructure, it places a component dedicated to the habits of workers, students, residents and people who visit the cross-border area.
| Plan | Content indicated in the project | |---|---| | Mobility supply | Routes, spaces and services for bicycles and walking | | Intermodality | Integration between public transport and cycling mobility | | Mobility demand | Information, awareness and propensity toward sustainable modes | | Planning | Analysis of the current state of affairs, volumes and emerging trends | | Pilot actions | Infrastructure, dedicated areas and training and awareness-raising initiatives |
The most direct connection for a cross-border commuter concerns the centrality of home-to-work travel. The project operates in an area that includes Varese, Como and Canton Ticino and considers daily mobility one of its areas of focus. The same approach also includes home-to-school travel and does not limit its scope to workers alone. The source also mentions tourism and leisure as components of daily traffic in the border area.
This distinction clarifies the scope of the initiative. SMILE is not presented as an intervention aimed at a single type of user or a single mode of transport. Active mobility includes cycling and walking, while intermodality connects these modes to public transport. The section dedicated to demand instead concerns knowledge and behavior, with information, training and awareness-raising activities.
A second strand concerns planning and experimentation. The Action Plan will have to build a shared vision, establish priorities and coordinate policies and actions along the border area. The pilot actions represent the operational step envisaged by the project: they will concern routes and areas for home-to-work and home-to-school travel, the enhancement of cycling services and initiatives aimed at mobility habits.
The source links the creation of SMILE to long-standing critical issues and congestion on the main roads, but does not provide measurements of travel times, the number of people involved or any reduction in traffic already achieved. The documented result is therefore the launch of a process of analysis, consultation and planning, not a quantitative effect that has already been verified.
For those who cross the border daily, the useful point is the decision to place home-to-work travel and intermodality at the center of the strategy. However, no definitive routes, schedules, kilometers of new infrastructure or methods for evaluating the effects of the pilot actions are indicated. ## The timing, participation, and limits of the information available
### From the conference to the cycle of meetings The calendar indicated by the source starts from Chiasso. On November 10, 2026, the conference will be open access and participation will be free. To take part in the event, an online registration is required through a special form.
The day will also have a participatory function. Local bodies, institutions and realities will be called upon to share priorities, critical issues, virtuous experiences and opportunities related to sustainable mobility. The dedicated working table will have to collect these contributions to guide the next phases of the project and the definition of the common strategy.
The process will go live between the end of November and the beginning of December 2026. In that period, a first cycle consisting of 6 operational meetings is planned. According to the source, these meetings are essential to develop a shared methodological approach in view of the final drafting of the Cross-border Action Plan.
This sequence makes it possible to distinguish what is already fixed from what must be defined. The place of the conference, the date, the free access, the registration route and the number of the first cycle of meetings are indicated. On the other hand, the names of the individual associated municipalities, the detailed calendar of meetings, the location of the pilot works or the number of routes and services that will be carried out are not reported.
### The perimeter of the source The text does not indicate a budget, an overall duration, kilometers of infrastructure, travel times or numerical targets on congestion. It also does not attribute to SMILE measures regarding G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, refunds, tax at source, New Frontier Agreement or double taxation. These issues remain outside the perimeter described, which concerns light mobility and the participation of actors in the border area.
The same caution applies to any connections with INPS or with specific places such as Brogeda: the source does not recall them and does not allow to attribute to the project interventions, procedures or effects on those references. For the border worker, the documented information therefore concerns the cross-border route on mobility, not taxation, social security or insurance.
The project, as it is presented, is still described through objectives, analysis, institutional comparison and pilot actions. The subsequent phases will have to translate this approach into a shared Plan and concrete interventions, but the source does not anticipate more specific content. For the topic of transport, please refer to the Ticino public transport.

item.title: Rome changes health tax proposal for former cross-border workers
item.description: Rome wants to change the rules of the so-called health tax before even applying it.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Rome changes the proposal before its implementation - The contribution would become fixed: 30-150 euros per month - The amount would be set every year by the Region - Ticino keeps just over 50 million frozen
Proposal → 2027 budget bill proposal Recipients → old cross-border workers in Italian border regions Amount → between 30 and 150 euros per month Calculation → fixed amount, not linked to Swiss salary Decision → Region of residence, every year Status → draft text
Rome wants to change the rules of the so-called health tax before even applying it. The change emerged on Monday from the draft of the 2027 budget bill and concerns a contribution that has existed since 2024.
State Councillor Christian Vitta comments on the Italian proposal and sees the change in approach as confirmation of the objections raised by Canton Ticino in recent months. The Ticino Government considers the criticism directed at the previous version to be well-founded.
Christian Vitta considers the change in the rules of the health tax confirmation of the validity of the positions supported by Canton Ticino in recent months: otherwise, it would be unclear why to intervene on a measure that has not yet been applied.
### The change in the draft The contribution concerns the so-called old cross-border workers: people who live in the Italian border regions and are taxed only in Switzerland. The amount is used to finance the Italian National Health Service.
The levy provided for under the current regulations is proportional to the Swiss salary, although the Regions have not applied it so far. In the draft, the criterion changes: the amount would be fixed, between 30 and 150 euros per month, and would be set every year by the Region in which one resides.
The director of the Department of Finance and Economy prefers not to comment on the details of the formula for now. For Canton Ticino, the issue is political: the tax would arrive shortly after the signing of an agreement between Switzerland and Italy, affecting a regulatory framework that has not yet been applied. The text is still a draft, and there is no indication that Parliament has made a final decision. ## From salary to a fixed amount
The difference between the two versions can be seen in the basis for the levy. Today, in the wording challenged by the Canton of Ticino, the amount depends proportionally on the Swiss salary; in the draft linked to the 2027 budget, the reference to salary disappears and a monthly range between 30 and 150 euros remains. The source does not indicate how the Region would choose the value within the range, nor what criteria it would use to set it each year.
The report refers to the so-called old cross-border workers. They are workers who live in the Italian border regions and who, for employment income, are taxed in Switzerland (for new cross-border workers, also in Italy, with a tax credit). From a tax perspective, Swiss withholding on employment income is a withholding tax. The healthcare contribution, by contrast, is presented as an amount intended for Italy’s National Health Service.
This distinction helps avoid confusing the healthcare levy with ordinary taxation of salary. It is precisely the addition of a further amount that fuels the objection raised by Cristian Bisa, of the Unione frontalieri italiani in Svizzera. For the trade unionist, changing the name does not change the substance: in his view, the request remains double taxation imposed on workers. The source also reports his objection concerning the service: it is decided how much and how to collect, but it is not indicated what would be offered to the worker in return.
| Version | Basis for the levy | Status | |---|---|---| | Current rule | Proportional to the Swiss salary | Challenged by the Canton of Ticino and never applied by the Regions | | 2027 proposal | Fixed amount between 30 and 150 euros per month | Included in the draft budget bill |
The political link indicated by Vitta is the agreement between Switzerland and Italy signed a short time ago. The source does not specify its contents or articles and does not explain how the new contribution would be coordinated with that agreement. The official legal reference for the agreement on cross-border workers is available in the [New Cross-Border Workers Agreement – Law 83/2023](https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:2023-06-13;83). The documented point in the article, however, remains the choice to propose a new tax after the agreement was signed, not the legal outcome of its review. ## Refurbishments and technical table
The question of the health tax does not change the Canton Ticino's route on refreshments. In June, the State Council blocked a part of the sums destined for Lombardy, a choice that the Federal Council had not shared.
Subsequently, Bern opened a working table with Rome involving the Lombardy Region and Canton Ticino. In the meantime, the funds remain blocked. Christian Vitta quantifies the frozen sum at just over 50 million and says that the Canton is ready to unlock it as soon as the technical table has completed its work.
### The draft and the required verifications On the revenue from the health tax, Vitta's position is clear: it is not good that everything goes to the Italian State; something, according to the Councilor of State, must also remain in the cantonal territory. It is a separate request from the monthly mechanism of the draft, because it concerns the destination of the revenue and not the way in which the amount is calculated.
Cristian Bisa maintains a principled critique. According to the representative of the Italian Border Union in Switzerland, a tax should correspond to a service. The text discussed, on the other hand, defines how much to withdraw and how to do it, while it does not indicate what would be done for the worker. The trade unionist therefore considers the simple change of words insufficient.
The procedure has not yet reached the final point: the text is a draft and the unions will ask for verification before approval. If Parliament gives the green light, they have announced that they will turn to the Public Prosecutor's Office. The source does not indicate the date of any vote or the outcome of the verification, so it does not yet document the application of the contribution or the date of a first payment.
As a separate official reference on the SSN fee, said health tax, is available on [DM Salute 14/11/2025](https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/gu/2025/12/18/293/sg/pdf). For refreshments chapter updates, see Ticino-Italy tax rebates.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4222865)*

item.title: Cross-border workers and teleworking: setting up a home workstation
item.description: Teleworking accounts for up to 25% of working time. The protocol entered into force on February 9, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Telework can account for up to 25% of working time. - The protocol entered into force on February 9, 2026. - Application begins on January 1, 2024. - The desk can also be used by the family.
## Key facts - Maximum share → 25% of working time - Effective → 9 February 2026 - Application → January 1, 2024 - Place of teleworking → the cross-border commuter's home - Work tool → computer provided by the company - Stable → connection for video calls and VPNs
Entered into force on 9 February 2026, the protocol updating the tax agreement between Italy and Switzerland on cross-border workers applies from 1 January 2024. The regulation allows you to work from your home for a maximum of 25% of your working time, without altering the tax regime or the status of cross-border commuter.
The source describes a possibility referring to thousands of cross-border workers in the province of Como. The limit is not equivalent to an entirely remote week: out of a normal five-day working week, 25% corresponds on average to just over one day. However, the count must be verified on the basis of actual working time and contractual situation.
### A ready-made and reversible place
To reduce the risk of errors in registration, it is useful to define with the employer how to record the days of teleworking and check the official indications relevant to your situation. The tax limit is distinct from the social security limit, which is subject to different rules. If doubts remain, you can ask for clarification from a patronage, a trade union or a tax advisor.
The regulatory part is directly linked to the practical question: how to prepare a workstation that will only be used for part of the week. Those who work from home only a few days rarely need a dedicated study. The desk can be placed in the living room, bedroom or corner of the house, and then used by the family on other days.
The workstation must offer a stable connection for video calls and corporate VPN, a screen suitable for several hours of work, a comfortable seat and proper lighting; the floor must be able to be set up in the morning and cleared in the evening. It is also preferable to minimize cables and bulky appliances. There is no need to transform the house into a copy of the office in Lugano or Mendrisio: all you need is a flexible desk, ready for the day of teleworking and usable even during the rest of the week. ## A compact desk, with two configurations
The most useful comparison is not between a home and a complete office, but between a dedicated workstation and a shared workstation. The source favors the latter: the work surface must be able to accommodate the company computer during teleworking and become available again for household use without multiplying screens, keyboards, and cables.
| Requirement | Solution described by the source | |---|---| | Low laptop screen | External monitor at eye level | | Spreadsheets and meetings | Multi-monitor setup | | Limited desk space | Monitor arm or stand | | Quick connection | Docking station or monitor with USB-C, if compatible | | Cables and power-off | Cable ducts, cable ties, and power strip with a switch |
The display should also be assessed in terms of comfort: after many hours, the laptop screen can be uncomfortable if it remains too low and forces the neck to tilt. Positioning an external monitor at eye level makes prolonged work easier. For those who alternate between spreadsheets, management software, and video calls, two monitors allow the documents to be displayed on one screen and the meeting on the second.
A mini PC can support two or more monitors at the same workstation, but it is first necessary to check which video outputs the model offers. If the work surface is small, a monitor arm or stand makes it possible to reclaim space. To connect the company laptop with a single cable, you can use a docking station or a monitor with a USB-C port, provided that the computer and monitor are compatible with this function.
To separate professional use from household use, the mini PC intended for the home can be placed behind the monitor, if compatible with a VESA mount, or under the desk. This way, the monitor, keyboard, and mouse remain usable with the company laptop as well. On teleworking days, it is sufficient to connect the work computer; on other days, the workstation can be used to browse the Internet, manage household matters, follow the children’s school activities, or video call relatives.
Switching between the two computers can be managed through a monitor with multiple inputs or a KVM switch, that is, a device that allows two machines to be controlled with the same keyboard and mouse. Sharing the workstation does not change the security rules: work must be carried out on the computer provided by the company, in compliance with its IT policies. Accessing company data from a private PC is often prohibited and may entail risks for both the worker and the employer.
Network stability also matters more than maximum speed. Fiber and FWA are both mentioned as possibilities, while an Ethernet connection or a Wi-Fi mesh system can help when the desk is far from the router. According to the text, it is advisable to test the company VPN in advance. ## The 25% scope and the necessary checks
The text distinguishes between two aspects that should not be conflated. On the one hand, there is the tax share of telework, set at up to 25% of working time; on the other, there is the social security threshold, which follows different rules. For this reason, the 25% figure is not presented as the same number of days for everyone, but as a limit to be assessed in relation to actual time and the contractual situation.
The two dates also serve different purposes. The protocol entered into force on February 9, 2026, while its application is stated to begin on January 1, 2024. The text does not turn this distinction into an individual calendar: it does not specify which days to choose, does not establish a fixed day of the week, and does not replace the agreement with the employer on recording attendance from home.
### What the source documents and what remains outside
The account focuses on telework and the setup of the workstation. It also does not address the New Cross-Border Agreement as a standalone topic, does not add data on Canton Ticino, and does not link the home workstation to the route to the Brogeda border crossing or to INPS procedures. These topics therefore remain outside the scope of the article and cannot be inferred from the telework share alone.
From an operational standpoint, the text suggests keeping a record of the days worked from home. The record serves to compare actual time with the applicable limit, without confusing the weekly average calculation with an automatic rule valid for every contract. In case of doubt, the indicated contacts are a social security assistance office, a trade union, and a tax adviser; the latest official guidance should be checked before planning the calendar, because the rules may be updated.
The same criterion applies to technology. The source describes external monitors, docking stations, stands, KVM switches, cable ducts, cable ties, and power strips with switches as solutions for a compact desk. It does not present them as a mandatory setup, nor does it specify a model, price, or configuration valid for everyone. The choice depends on compatibility among the laptop, monitor, video outputs, VESA mount, and available connections.
For the tax framework alone, one of the available official references is the [AFC information sheet](https://m4.ti.ch/fileadmin/DFE/DC/DOC-IF/nuovo_accordo/nuovo_accordo_foglio_informativo_FAQ.pdf). The source on the workstation nevertheless stresses the need to check the most recent official guidance and to separate the tax issue from the social security issue.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/pubbliredazionale/frontalieri-e-telelavoro-nel-2026-come-organizzare-la-postazione-di-lavoro-a-casa/)*
